questions.answer: For a \(2\times 2\) matrix \(A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\), the adjugate swaps the diagonal entries and changes the signs of the off-diagonal entries. Therefore adj(A) = \(\begin{pmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}\).
Use the \(2\times 2\) adjugate rule. Swap the diagonal entries 1 and 4, and change signs of the off-diagonal entries 2 and 3. Therefore adj(A) = \(\begin{pmatrix}4&-2\\-3&1\end{pmatrix}\).

First compute \(\det(A)\) = \(1\cdot4\) - \(2\cdot3\) = -2. The adjugate is \(\begin{pmatrix}4&-2\\-3&1\end{pmatrix}\). The inverse formula is \(A^{-1}\) = (1/\(\det(A)\)) adj(A). Therefore \(A^{-1}\) = (-1/2)\(\begin{pmatrix}4&-2\\-3&1\end{pmatrix}\) = \(\begin{pmatrix}-2&1\\3/2&-1/2\end{pmatrix}\).

For \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}\), \(\det(A)\) = -2 and adj(A) = \(\begin{pmatrix}4&-2\\-3&1\end{pmatrix}\). Multiply: A adj(A) = \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&4\end{pmatrix}\)\(\begin{pmatrix}4&-2\\-3&1\end{pmatrix}\). The entries are top-left 4 - 6 = -2, top-right -2 + 2 = 0, bottom-left 12 - 12 = 0, bottom-right -6 + 4 = -2. Thus A adj(A) = \(\begin{pmatrix}-2&0\\0&-2\end{pmatrix}\) = \(\det(A)\)I.

questions.prompt: Explain why the adjugate formula cannot produce an inverse when \(\det(A)\) = 0.
questions.answer: The adjugate inverse formula is \(A^{-1}\) = (1/\(\det(A)\))adj(A). If \(\det(A)\) = 0, this formula requires division by zero, which is undefined. This matches the invertibility test: a square matrix with determinant zero has no inverse.

questions.prompt: Find all t such that \(A=\begin{pmatrix}t&1\\2&1\end{pmatrix}\) has adj(A) = \(\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\-2&t\end{pmatrix}\).
questions.answer: For \(\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\), adj(A) = \(\begin{pmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}\). For \(A=\begin{pmatrix}t&1\\2&1\end{pmatrix}\), this gives adj(A) = \(\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\-2&t\end{pmatrix}\). This matches the given adjugate for every real t. Therefore all real t work.
The determinant is \(0\cdot1\) - \(2\cdot5\) = -10. The adjugate swaps the diagonal entries and negates the off-diagonal entries, so adj(A) = \(\begin{pmatrix}1&-2\\-5&0\end{pmatrix}\).

questions.prompt: A learner says adj(\(\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\)) = \(\begin{pmatrix}d&c\\b&a\end{pmatrix}\). Diagnose the error.
questions.answer: The learner swapped the diagonal entries but forgot to change the signs of the off-diagonal entries. The correct formula is adj(\(\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}\)) = \(\begin{pmatrix}d&-b\\-c&a\end{pmatrix}\). The off-diagonal entries b and c must become -b and -c.
